title: Coefficient/exponent pair (4, 1) with explicit remainder 60*n^(4/5)+10 for the fixed BK/Shoup family

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. The fixed algorithm and field basis are as specified in proof.md.","guarantee":{"kind":"eventual_lower_bound","leading":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"remainder":{"kind":"explicit","terms":[{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"60"},"exponent":{"denominator":"5","numerator":"4"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"10"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}}]}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one total uniform polynomial-time family, hence in NP with empty witnesses, for every integer n>=1, C_B2(f_n)>=4n-10*d(n) with d(n)=floor(6*n^(4/5))+1, and therefore C_B2(f_n)>=4n-60*n^(4/5)-10, at actual input length n=|x| in the full Li-Yang B2 model. Hence liminf C_B2(f_n)/n>=4.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v2"}

claims: Unscored lemma (Theorem G of proof.md): for every integer n>=1, every Boolean function f:{0,1}^n->{0,1} that is an affine disperser for a dimension d>=1 (nonconstant on every d-dimensional affine subspace of F_2^n) satisfies C_B2(f)>=4n-10d for every B_2 circuit computing f, where d is that dimension. This lemma is proved in full in Sections 4-9 of proof.md and is the engine of the main theorem; it is declared unscored and supplies neither score coordinate.
